input_ref.x-reference-rule: Allow-listed scheme AND constrained body, identical to the CTR-IDM-001 result_ref rule. The earlier constraint was a deny-list, not:{pattern:"^https?://"}, which matched only a literal lowercase http(s) prefix. Independent security review, reproduced by WP-0A-CON-005 against the shipped schema, passed ALL of: HTTPS://public.example.invalid/x (uppercase scheme), //public.example.invalid/x (protocol-relative authority), ftp://public.example.invalid/x, data:text/plain;base64,AA==, file:///etc/passwd, javascript:alert(1) and ../../../etc/passwd. A scheme allow-list alone is also not enough: with a free body it would still pass result:../../../etc/passwd, status:/proc/self/environ, content:/.env and content://attacker.example.invalid/exfil. A leading slash, any `..` segment, an empty segment and an authority are all rejected. The scheme list is closed. The two negative lookaheads were removed: a 400,000-string fuzz by independent testing found zero divergence from this lookahead-free form, because the body grammar already forbids a leading slash, an empty segment and a `..` segment. Removing them closes WP-0A-CON-002 review finding R8 (RE2 portability) at zero cost, which had no recorded disposition anywhere.
input_ref.x-minlength-note: `minLength` was REMOVED as unreachable: no single character matches this pattern, checked over every code point below U+2100, so no instance can distinguish this schema from one without it. Keeping a constraint nothing can exercise inflates every coverage number that counts it and reads as a defence it is not.

x-lifecycle.decided: 2026-10-20, by the contract owner A0 in WP-0A-CON-001, on the Product Owner's direction of 2026-10-20 (evidence/WP-0A-CON-001/product-owner-disposition-2026-10-20-ctr-job-lifecycle.md): the lifecycle is what platform-kernel's job decisions already decide (src/modules/platform-kernel/domain/jobs/job-decisions.ts at main f20b7319), named. While this contract is Candidate it may change; once it is Frozen, changing a state, the order of `states` or a transition is a breaking change (RFC-2026-031 section 3.3).
x-lifecycle.stored: No state is stored. The record has no status field and gains none (additionalProperties is false). A job's state is derived at an instant `now` that its reader supplies, from the record's timestamps and counters, as the FIRST entry of `states` whose condition holds. The same record can therefore be in different states at different instants: time alone moves a job (`by: clock`), with no write.
x-lifecycle.lease_held: lease_owner and lease_expires_at are both present and lease_expires_at > now. A lease whose lease_expires_at <= now is expired: it protects nothing, and its two fields stay on the record until the next claim replaces them.

states.when: cancel_requested_at is present and the lease is held
none of the above: no result, no cancellation, no held lease, attempt < max_attempts and available_at <= now; the only state a claim is granted from

actors.command: The command path, inside the job's own workspace only: enqueue, with a tenant context the resolver minted, and cancel. How the database admits the command path is not settled here.
actors.worker: A worker, only through the queue broker in the database (RFC-2026-022 section 5 items 5 and 6: functions owned by app_queue; app_worker holds no policy on app.jobs) and through JobStorePort on fakes. Every act after a claim presents the lease the claim returned (job_id, workspace_id, lease_owner, attempt), and is refused with nothing written (lease_lost) unless that lease is held and is the record's current one.
actors.clock: No actor and no write: the instant reaching available_at or lease_expires_at.

transitions.writes: A new record: attempt 0, progress_percent 0, no lease, no cancel_requested_at, no result_ref, no last_error_code. available_at is the requested instant, or now when absent or earlier, so the job is ready at now or waiting until later. When a job with the same dedupe_key exists in the same workspace, nothing is written and that job is returned in whatever state it is.
attempt + 1; lease_owner; lease_expires_at = now + timeout_seconds + the lease grace. Refused, with nothing written, from every other state.
lease_expires_at = the later of its current value and now + the heartbeat extension; progress_percent and progress_stage when given, with no requirement that progress increase.

last_error_code, the code of a stable error defined in code; the lease is removed; available_at = now + min(maximum delay, base delay * factor ^ (attempt - 1)). Every failure is retried while attempts remain, whatever its error's `retryable`.
last_error_code; the lease is removed; available_at is unchanged.
As the two rows above, by attempt; the cancellation decides the state.
Nothing. ready when attempt < max_attempts, otherwise dead_lettered. This is how a crashed worker's job is taken again, so a handler may run more than once (at least once).
cancel_requested_at = now. The held lease runs to its end, and heartbeats may extend it.
Nothing; the first instant is kept.

x-lifecycle.never: No act changes the state of a completed or cancelled job, and only cancel moves a dead_lettered one. After enqueue: only claim writes attempt and lease_owner; only claim and heartbeat write lease_expires_at; only complete and fail remove the lease; only heartbeat writes progress_percent and progress_stage; only complete writes result_ref; only fail writes last_error_code and available_at; only cancel writes cancel_requested_at. No replay is defined.
not_settled: The numbers: the lease grace, the heartbeat extension, the back-off base, factor and maximum, and the enqueue caps on max_attempts and timeout_seconds are D6 provisional kernel parameters (src/modules/platform-kernel/domain/jobs/job-limits.ts), not contract values.

A retry taxonomy by error category (Contracts/Events/Jobs Workstream JB-005: validation and auth errors not retried, Retry-After honoured) is not adopted: every failure is retried while attempts remain.
Cancellation does not reach a running handler: the worker aborts a handler at its timeout only (JB-006 asks for a safe point).
Progress is not required to be monotonic (JB-007).
Dead-letter triage and replay (JB-009), and the controlled replay JB-001 excepts from terminal immutability.
The order in which ready jobs are claimed (the direction of priority, and ties).
Retention, archival and cleanup of terminal jobs (JB-010).
